newsitem.title: CHINA: HK spent US$1.0 bln defending HK dollar in July.
newsitem.headline: HK spent US$1.0 bln defending HK dollar in July.

text.p: The Hong Kong government spent US$1.0 billion from its reserves fending off speculative attacks against the Hong Kong dollar in July, a government spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
"Everything was resolved in a very swift manner," she said.

Hong Kong government radio earlier quoted Financial Secretary Donald Tsang as saying that the government had repelled the attack against the Hong Kong dollar in about two hours on an unspecified day in July, spending US$1.0 billion.

The Hong Kong dollar has been pegged at HK$7.8 to the U.S. dollar since the currency plunged in 1983 due to worries over the future of the former British colony, which returned to China in June this year.
Several Asian currencies have been targeted by speculators over the last several weeks in the wake of Thailand's currency and financial crisis.
The spokeswoman said the government also knew the identity of the speculator, but said Tsang had declined to identify the attacker.

Another government official, who declined to be named, told Reuters that whatever the authorities might have spent on defending the currency was not lost because the government could reverse its position in the market later once currency volatility had eased.
Hong Kong foreign exchange dealers said the local currency held up well on Tuesday despite heavy selling of other Asian currencies, notably the Singapore dollar.
"The Hong Kong dollar was little changed despite the drop in the Singapore dollar and other Asian currencies, though there was some movement in the forward rates," said one dealer.
"The market is very concerned about the HKMA (Hong Kong Monetary Authority) coming in because they are very serious (about defending the currency)," he said.
But there was no sign of intervention in Tuesday's session, the dealer said.
The Hong Kong dollar was trading at HK$7.7433/43 to the dollar.
